# containerkit

> Emit containerkit instead of a Compose file, a Dockerfile, and a shell script that drift apart. One program is the Engine SDK and the Compose SDK, in Go and in TSX.

Emit containerkit instead. The configuration and the operations are one program: the same names in Go and in TSX for a service, a volume, a network, a secret, a build, an image, a Swarm object, and a `pull`. The components and session methods are generated from the kit against pinned Moby and Compose SDKs, so configuration follows typed mappings rather than guessed YAML keys. `exportYAML` on a named `Compose` and `exportDockerfile` on a `Dockerfile` return the file text without dialing the daemon and without stopping a session. A live `docker.ts` default-exports `root()`, keeps the session open, and applies the project only when the rendered YAML changes. `AsService` copies a container spec onto a Compose service, and `Validate` reports unsupported mappings. A Dockerfile is its own tree in `containerkit/dockerfile`: `<Run>` joins a layer, `<RunLayer>` starts the next. Named constants (`proto`, `restartPolicy`, and the rest) come from `containerkit/vocab`.

```tsx
import { Compose, Service, Publish, exportYAML } from "containerkit";
import { proto } from "containerkit/vocab";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Compose name="app">
      <Service
        name="api"
        image="alpine:latest"
        command={["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo ok > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]}
      >
        <Publish hostPort={8080} containerPort={80} protocol={proto.TCP} />
      </Service>
    </Compose>
  );
}

export const yaml = exportYAML(<App />);
```

Emit that module. `exportYAML` returns the Compose text. `httpd` serves `/www/index.html`, which the command creates, and publishes `8080` to `80`. For a process that stays up, default-export `root()` from `containerkit/live` in a file named `docker.ts`. Inside that function, `const app = useSession()` is the session:

```tsx
import { Compose, Service, Publish } from "containerkit";
import { proto } from "containerkit/vocab";
import { root, useMemo, useSession } from "containerkit/live";

export default root({ fromEnv: true }, function App() {
  const app = useSession();
  const ready = useMemo(() => app.pullImage("alpine:latest"), ["alpine:latest"]);
  if (!ready) return null;
  return (
    <Compose name="app">
      <Service
        name="api"
        image="alpine:latest"
        command={["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo ok > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]}
      >
        <Publish hostPort={8080} containerPort={80} protocol={proto.TCP} />
      </Service>
    </Compose>
  );
});
```

`useSession()` is legal only while that function is rendering. Pins verified 2026-11-12: `github.com/moby/moby/api` v1.56.1, `github.com/moby/moby/client` v0.6.2, `github.com/compose-spec/compose-go/v2` v2.16.2, `github.com/docker/compose/v5` v5.6.1.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): The project as components, the live session, the same names in Go, and how regeneration tracks the pinned SDKs. “A container becomes a service” is where `Validate` names each unsupported mapping.
- [TSX docs](tsx/docs/README.md): Reading order for a TypeScript user. Trees, the live session, the client, commands, then Dockerfiles.
- [Trees](tsx/docs/trees.md): Writing the project as components and exporting YAML from a named Compose node.
- [Live session](tsx/docs/live.md): `docker.ts`, `root()`, re-render, and applying the project only when the rendered YAML changes.
- [Commands](tsx/docs/commands.md): Session methods for images, containers, networks, volumes, Swarm, and Compose.
- [Dockerfiles](tsx/docs/dockerfile.md): The Dockerfile tree, `Run` and `RunLayer`, and `exportDockerfile`.
- [Client](tsx/docs/client.md): Which daemon the session talks to. `connect` records settings and does not dial by itself.

## Examples

- [Supabase in TSX](tsx/examples/supabase.tsx): A full Compose project — gateway, Postgres, pooler, storage, logs — printed as YAML on stdout.
- [Image](tsx/examples/image.tsx): A multi-stage Dockerfile whose stages and layers follow the environment, printed on stdout.
- [Taskflow in TSX](tsx/examples/taskflow.tsx): A release graph. The image build overlaps Postgres. Lint waits for that image, then overlaps the database. Migrate retries. A failed check skips the tag. Down waits only for migrate, because unit and lint do not use Postgres, and still runs when migrate fails. Stdout is the plan document.
- [Supabase in Go](examples/supabase): The same stack written with the Go kit.

## Optional

- [TSX package README](tsx/README.md): Install, Node 20, and `containerkit/tsconfig.jsx.json` so `<Compose>` needs no per-file JSX pragma.
- [TSX guide](tsx/GUIDE.md): Longer list of prop names and command names.
- [Declare config in TSX](docs/tsx-configuration.md): How a folder is set up to compile containerkit JSX.
- [Publish a port](docs/publish-a-port.md): Port mappings.
- [Mount a volume](docs/mount-a-volume.md): Volumes and mounts.
- [Bring a compose file up](docs/bring-a-compose-file-up.md): Applying a project.
- [Taskflow](docs/taskflow.md): An optional DAG of container, build, and Compose steps, including the TypeScript `Flow` document.
- [Runner binary](docs/runner-binary.md): The `containerkit` binary a live session starts. Build it with `go run ./tools/crossbuild`.
